extra.department: Mayor's Office of Education (Office of Adult Education)
extra.what: Trains volunteers to tutor adult learners in reading, math, digital skills or English for speakers of other languages, at one of about 20 myPLACE network providers citywide.
extra.who_can_join: unknown, not confirmed on a page we fetched
extra.training: Yes: a free 10 to 12 hour training before being matched with a learner
extra.clearances: Unknown in detail; a 'Step-By-Step Guide to Completing Clearances' for Adult Ed volunteers exists on phila.gov but we did not fetch its contents this pass
extra.notes: Contact is the hotline (833) 750-5627 or adultedu@phila.gov. A 2022-08-15 post said 86 volunteers completed training in one recent year, with 50 referred to providers.

extra.department: Department of Sanitation (Philadelphia More Beautiful Committee)
extra.what: Lets any resident organize their block, collect signatures from 51 percent of their neighbors on a petition, and then run block cleanups with the Philadelphia More Beautiful Committee.
extra.who_can_join: any resident
extra.notes: Contact to request a petition is PMBC at (215) 685-3971, or an online form on the same page.

name: Business and individual volunteer opportunities (Parks and Recreation)

extra.department: Philadelphia Parks and Recreation
extra.what: The general entry point for weeding, planting, trail clearing, rec center after school help and special event volunteering such as the Broad Street Run, outside of a specific Friends group.
extra.who_can_join: Any resident or group; an ongoing rec center or playground role needs background clearances
extra.clearances: Background clearances required for an ongoing position at a playground or rec center, per PPR's volunteer clearance policy
extra.notes: Individuals sign up for the second Saturday of every month at loveyourpark.org; community and corporate groups fill out a Google form on the same page.

extra.department: Philadelphia Police Department
extra.what: A ten week evening course, run each fall at the Police Academy, that teaches residents how police operate.
extra.who_can_join: unknown, not confirmed by a page we could fetch
extra.commitment: Weekly for about 10 weeks, one evening a week, seasonal (fall)
extra.training: n/a, the course is the training
extra.notes: We could not find or guess a current standalone phila.gov page with sign up instructions (several likely URLs returned 404). What is known (10 Wednesday evenings, 6:30 to 9:30 pm, contact a named officer at the Police Academy) comes from indexed search result text about a Citizens Police Oversight Commission presentation to an academy class, not a page we read ourselves. Evidence date is weak; worth a phone check before publishing with confidence.

name: City boards and commissions, resident seats

extra.department: Office of the Chief Integrity Officer
extra.what: A public directory of the City's advisory boards and commissions, for example the Civic Design Review Board, the Housing Advisory Board and the Commission on Faith Based and Interfaith Affairs, most unpaid, that a resident can ask to serve on.
extra.who_can_join: Varies by board; most members are mayor appointed rather than open sign up
extra.commitment: Varies by board, typically monthly or quarterly meetings
extra.notes: This is an index of many boards, not one single program; included because the task specifically asked about resident seats on boards and commissions. Questions go to CityBoards@phila.gov; we found no page describing a general application process beyond that contact.

extra.department: Office of the City Commissioners
extra.what: Appointed residents staff the City's 1,703 voting divisions on election day, opening and closing polling places and checking in voters.
extra.who_can_join: qualified electors of Philadelphia
extra.training: Yes: required training before election day
extra.notes: Poll workers are paid a stipend (Judges of Election are paid $215 per election day), so this is a paid civic role rather than a pure volunteer shift; included because the task named it by name. The page carried no machine readable "last updated" date, unlike the main phila.gov template.

extra.department: Philadelphia Fire Department
extra.what: A two year program for teens that teaches firefighting and EMS basics through Saturday training at the Fire Academy and counts toward civil service exam points.
extra.who_can_join: 14 to 20 years old, enrolled in at least 9th grade by the program's April start date, parent or guardian consent required if under 18
extra.commitment: Every other Saturday, 9 am to 5 pm, April through November, for a two year commitment
extra.training: Yes: classroom instruction and hands on training from local and state agencies
extra.clearances: None stated; requires good physical health, English literacy, and a signed consent form
extra.notes: The program's own page has not been updated since 2018, but a 2024-04-09 City summer programs roundup still promotes it, so we treat it as active with that caveat. Contact per the page's application flow is PFDrecruitment@phila.gov.

extra.department: Office of Children and Families, Department of Human Services
extra.what: Pays a stipend to income eligible seniors who volunteer 15 to 40 hours a week mentoring children ages 3 to 7 in Philadelphia Pre-K and elementary classrooms, as part of the national AmeriCorps Seniors network.
extra.who_can_join: 55 or older, limited income, must live in Philadelphia
extra.training: Yes: an information session and an orientation
extra.clearances: PA Child Abuse History Clearance, PA State Police Criminal Record Check, FBI Criminal History Background Check, and a National Sex Offender public website check
extra.notes: Philadelphia's is described on the page as one of the oldest and largest Foster Grandparent programs of its kind. serve.phila.gov, the City's old general volunteer portal address, now redirects to the Office of Community Empowerment and Opportunity's department page rather than to this program; Foster Grandparents itself is run by DHS's Office of Children and Families, not OCEO.

extra.department: Free Library of Philadelphia
extra.what: Places volunteers at library branches as computer tutors for older adults, English conversation group facilitators, and after school program leaders for teens.
extra.who_can_join: Varies by role; teen volunteer roles are open to students in grades 7 through 12
extra.notes: freelibrary.org returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, and this phila.gov subdomain (libwww.library.phila.gov) timed out on every attempt rather than connecting at all. Per the project's rule never to work around a block, everything in this entry comes from phila.gov indexed search result text, not a page we read ourselves, so treat the details as lower confidence than our other entries. "Friends of the Free Library of Philadelphia" also appears to exist as an organization, mentioned in passing in one search result, but we could not confirm current chapter details this pass.

extra.department: Philadelphia Parks and Recreation, with Fairmount Park Conservancy and the Park Friends Network
extra.what: A citywide week of park cleanup and care days each spring, plus a Fall Service Day, run jointly by the City and park partner organizations.
extra.who_can_join: any resident
extra.season: Spring (a week) and one day each fall
extra.notes: The 2026 Love Your Park Week ran May 9 to 17, across more than 100 Philadelphia parks.

extra.department: n/a. Mural Arts Philadelphia is an independent nonprofit, not a City department; it is a long time City partner on public art
extra.what: An independent nonprofit that runs Philadelphia's public mural and community art programs and recruits volunteers for mural painting days.
extra.who_can_join: unknown
extra.notes: Listed only as a link, per the project's rule to never copy a nonprofit partner's own text and to link, not research, a partner organization in depth. Not counted in the City program total in the harvest report, since it is not City government.

extra.department: Philadelphia Parks and Recreation (Stewardship Office), with Fairmount Park Conservancy
extra.what: Connects residents to one of more than 100 community led Friends groups that clean, program and advocate for their local park.
extra.who_can_join: any resident
extra.notes: Contact to connect with a group is the Stewardship Office, (215) 683-3679 or PPRstewardship@phila.gov.

extra.department: Department of Public Health
extra.what: Registers and trains medical, public health and support volunteers that the Department of Public Health deploys during public health emergencies and large City events.
extra.who_can_join: 18 or older; must live in Philadelphia
extra.training: Yes: trainings, exercises and real deployment opportunities offered throughout the year
extra.clearances: A criminal background check; licensed medical volunteers must hold an active, unencumbered license
extra.notes: The program page says it currently has over 7,000 members. Also reachable through the Office of Emergency Management's "Volunteering" referral page, which otherwise just links out to independent emergency response organizations rather than running its own corps.

name: Philadelphia More Beautiful Committee Clean Block Program

extra.department: Department of Sanitation
extra.what: Each year the Department of Sanitation partners with block captains for organized Saturday cleanups by police district, plus an annual Clean Block Contest with cash prizes for the cleanest blocks.
extra.who_can_join: block captains and their neighbors
extra.season: Spring and fall; the 2025 contest was judged over three Saturdays in September and October
extra.notes: The 2024 season reported 9,207 blocks cleaned by 25,877 PMBC volunteers. Works alongside the block captain program above.

extra.department: Office of the Chief Integrity Officer (Boards and Commissions)
extra.what: An advisory body of young Philadelphians who comment on City youth policy, help create youth programs and partner with youth organizations.
extra.who_can_join: Youth resident members, appointed; the directory page does not state an age range or a public application form
extra.notes: Listed alongside dozens of other advisory boards and commissions on the same directory page; general questions go to CityBoards@phila.gov. No separate public application page was found this pass.

extra.department: Office of Children and Families, Department of Human Services (Out of School Time)
extra.what: Pairs a trained volunteer with a K to 3rd grade student for weekly one on one after school reading sessions at an Out of School Time site, October through May.
extra.who_can_join: 16 or older (16 to 17 year olds need a parent or guardian waiver); no residency requirement stated
extra.training: Yes: an orientation plus a Safe Schools mandated reporter training module
extra.clearances: PA State Criminal Background Check, PA Child Abuse History Clearance, an FBI waiver or fingerprint check, a City Release Waiver (18+) or Parental Release Waiver (16 to 17), and a National Sex Offender Registry check for adults
extra.notes: A 2023-11-27 phila.gov news post first announced the program, but its own site on the Out of School Time subdomain (ost.phila.gov) is the current, more detailed source: as of this research pass it said it is "now accepting volunteers for the 2026-2027 school year."

extra.department: Office of Clean and Green Initiatives
extra.what: The City's largest single day citywide cleanup, where residents and organizations register a project or sign up to help with an existing one.
extra.who_can_join: any resident or organization
extra.notes: Since its 2008 launch the event reports 200,000 total volunteers and 11.4 million pounds of trash removed. The 2026 event was held April 11. At the time of this research pass the registration page said registration was closed, which is normal outside the weeks leading up to the annual event, not a sign the program ended.

extra.department: Office of Homeless Services
extra.what: Recruits several hundred trained volunteers for one night each January to canvass the city overnight and count and survey people experiencing unsheltered homelessness.
extra.who_can_join: any resident
extra.training: Yes: volunteers are trained the same day or before the count
extra.notes: The count is a federally required annual event, so it almost certainly ran again in January 2025 and 2026, but we did not find a newer phila.gov recap post in this research pass; the 2024 recap (more than 360 volunteers) is the newest dated evidence we have.

extra.department: Philadelphia Police Department
extra.what: A program for teens considering a police career, teaching law enforcement skills through mentoring, classroom instruction and hands on training.
extra.who_can_join: Reported as 14 to 20 years old in indexed search text; not independently confirmed on a page we fetched
extra.commitment: A two year commitment, per indexed search text
extra.training: Yes: classroom instruction and hands on training
extra.notes: Contact per search text is Police.Explorers@phila.gov. We tried several guessed URL patterns for a dedicated enrollment page (all 404) and could not confirm one by direct fetch, so the age range and commitment length above carry lower confidence than our other entries; treat them as reported, not verified.

extra.department: Office of Innovation and Technology
extra.what: Trains volunteers to work as digital skills coaches, lab monitors and classroom aides, helping Philadelphia residents build computer and internet skills at library, Parks and Recreation, and Adult Education sites.
extra.who_can_join: 14 or older (14 to 17 year olds need parent or guardian permission); no residency requirement stated
extra.training: Yes: a 20 minute screening call plus an orientation module
extra.clearances: PA Criminal History Background Check and PA Child Abuse Clearance for anyone working with youth or at a Parks and Recreation or Free Library site; some sites also want an FBI check, which is waived for Pennsylvania residents of more than 10 consecutive years
extra.notes: Launched per a 2026-01-29 announcement. As of this research pass the application form was temporarily closed because the program said it was at capacity for volunteers and asked people to check back in a few weeks, so the program itself is active even though new sign ups were paused that day.

extra.department: Philadelphia Parks and Recreation
extra.what: Lets anyone become a voting member of their local rec center's advisory council just by attending one meeting and signing in, with elected officer roles for more involved members.
extra.who_can_join: Any resident; officer roles need to be 18 and meet attendance and participation rules
extra.notes: Connect through the recreation facility closest to you, using the Parks and Rec facility finder.

name: School District of Philadelphia classroom volunteers

extra.department: School District of Philadelphia, Family and Community Engagement (FACE). FLAGGED: public agency, not City government
extra.what: Lets a resident volunteer in a Philadelphia public school classroom after checking with that school and completing a free Pennsylvania Child Abuse History Clearance.
extra.who_can_join: any resident willing to complete the required clearance
extra.clearances: Pennsylvania Child Abuse History Clearance (free for volunteers); the page also points to a separate volunteer checklist we did not fetch, which may name further clearances
extra.notes: The School District of Philadelphia is a separate public agency from the City of Philadelphia government, with its own elected Board of Education; it is not a City department. Included, and flagged, because the task asked for it to be checked.

extra.department: Office of Community Empowerment and Opportunity
extra.what: Places full time AmeriCorps VISTA members for a year of paid, stipend supported national service inside City offices, for example the Office of Immigrant Affairs.
extra.who_can_join: unknown, not confirmed on a phila.gov page this pass
extra.season: Year round; a new VISTA class typically starts late summer
extra.notes: This is a full time, stipend supported national service year, not a casual volunteer shift. Included because it is the City's own structured "join and serve" program and because the task asked specifically about the Office of Community Empowerment and Opportunity. The Office of Immigrant Affairs itself also occasionally recruits ad hoc legal volunteers (for example "Know Your Rights" presenters) but we found no standing, structured public sign up for that beyond VISTA, so it is not listed as its own entry.

extra.department: Philadelphia Water Department
extra.what: Gives small grants to community organizations that adopt and maintain a rain garden or other green stormwater site the Water Department built in their area.
extra.who_can_join: 501(c)(3) organizations with at least one paid staff member (or equivalent) and existing Water Department green infrastructure in their service area; not open to individual residents applying directly
extra.training: Yes: a training session and a site tour
extra.notes: A resident cannot adopt a site alone. The way an individual resident takes part is by joining one of the adopting civic or community groups' cleanup days, not by applying to the Water Department directly. Evidence date is weak (the site's own copyright footer reads "2018 to 2026"); we did not find a more precisely dated page this pass.

extra.department: Office of Public Safety (Town Watch Integrated Services)
extra.what: Trains, equips and certifies neighborhood Town Watch groups that patrol and report on their blocks, and runs Citizens Emergency Response Training (CERT), which teaches groups what to do in a disaster.
extra.who_can_join: any resident, through an existing or newly certified Town Watch group
extra.training: Yes: TWIS trains and certifies groups, including CERT disaster training
extra.clearances: unknown, not stated on this page
extra.notes: This is the City's answer to the task's "CERT" checklist item. The Office of Emergency Management's own "Volunteering" page does not run a CERT program itself; CERT is one of TWIS's support programs, alongside Safe Corridors and drug prevention and anti bullying programs. A new group applies with a form linked from this page; an individual resident joins an existing group, not a citywide roster.

extra.department: Philadelphia Parks and Recreation (Philly Tree Plan)
extra.what: The City's free yard tree giveaway program looks for volunteers to help run its spring and fall giveaway events.
extra.who_can_join: any resident
extra.notes: The Philly Tree Plan resources page itself was last updated 2023-02, but the Parks and Recreation volunteering page (lastUpdated 2026-09) still actively promotes TreePhilly giveaway volunteering, so we use that as the better evidence date. The City's own page points residents who want deeper tree care training to the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society's Tree Tenders program; that program belongs to PHS, a nonprofit partner, not the City, so it is not a separate City program entry here.

extra.department: Philadelphia Department of Prisons
extra.what: Trains volunteers to provide educational and spiritual support to people held at one of four Philadelphia Department of Prisons facilities.
extra.who_can_join: 21 or older, valid state ID; if formerly incarcerated, must wait six months after release
extra.training: Yes: 16 hours with the PDP training academy
extra.clearances: A background check, subject to the Commissioner of Prisons' approval
extra.notes: A 2024-10-30 post also promoted the program to university students and local residents.
